scene: Episode 02 · Scene 17 — EXT. HESSEL PIER — RECIPROCITY HOUSE — THE TRUE SENTENCE
shot: v4: opens on Beatrice's hand in the slot with the light dying (the threat, finally visible); Tomas lifts her hand out the way he lifted Pikk's in Sc08, puts his own in, and nothing happens; the six words; his breath; the slot takes it; the doorway rises to white. Tomas large in Shot 3 (§143); doorway named in both states (§147).
prompt:
Live-action mythic modernism. Photoreal, tactile, cinematic, anamorphic widescreen, 24fps, shallow depth of field. FOUR SHOTS, cut in camera at the stated times, and no other coverage. All spoken dialogue is in ENGLISH.

CAMERA DOCTRINE: SHOTS 1 AND 3 EACH CARRY ONE slow, smooth, continuous, dead-steady MECHANICAL DOLLY MOVE at a constant speed, still moving when the shot cuts; NOT handheld. SHOT 2 IS LOCKED. SHOT 4 IS ABSOLUTELY LOCKED and REFUSES TO MOVE TO THE GOOD NEWS HAPPENING BEHIND IT.

REFERENCE PRECEDENCE: @Image1 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE CHAMBER. @Image2 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE STONE AND THE SLOTS. @Image3 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THE PIER seen through the doorway. @Image4 IS THE AUTHORITY FOR HOW BEATRICE LOOKS WITH THE FROST ON HER — rime on the back of her right hand, a small starburst at the base of her throat.

THE CHAMBER: a small round room of COARSE, COLD, WEATHERED DARK GREY GRANITE, almost charcoal in shadow, salt-stained and pitted, laid in large heavy irregular blocks — NOT pale, NOT cream, NOT limestone. A row of small HORIZONTAL openings, each a hand's width across and only a few centimetres high, is cut into the curved wall at waist height with a thin warm amber light deep inside each one. Directly under them the stone sill is hollowed into a long smooth trough by four hundred years of hands. One stone bench. One plain doorway onto a flat white sky and the frozen pier. NO MACHINERY ANYWHERE.

TWO PRACTICAL LIGHT SOURCES, NEVER BLENDED, NEITHER WITH A VISIBLE FIXTURE: COLD blue-white 6500K daylight through the doorway, and WARM amber 3200K from deep inside the slots.

THE RULE OF THE SLOT LIGHT, established earlier and used here: when a slot is DRAWING from the hand in it, the amber light inside that slot DIMS for as long as the draw lasts; when a slot is taking NOTHING, its light stays STEADY and unchanged. It is a practical lamp on a dimmer: it never flashes, strobes, pulses or burns brighter.

THE SLOTS BEGIN THIS FILM DIM — barely lit, about a third of their normal strength. A FAINT DRY TICK comes from the rank each time it draws; it runs from the first frame until the moment stated in Shot 4, and then it stops.

CAST — ONLY TWO PEOPLE APPEAR. A woman's voice is heard from outside and she is never seen.
@Image5 and @Image6 are BEATRICE MORD — a WOMAN in her early forties, dark hair in a TIGHT HIGH TOPKNOT, clean-shaven, in a BLACK ASYMMETRICAL WRAP COAT wrapped and belted across the body over a full-length OXBLOOD-AND-RUST underskirt panel. She has NO cream panel, NO tall collar, NO cuffs, NO ribbon, NO blue, NO rust sash, NO leather chest strap, NO glass cylinders, NO earrings and NO veil. THE FROST IS ON HER, exactly as @Image4.
@Image7 and @Image8 are TOMAS GREY — a MAN in his thirties, tall, OLIVE-SKINNED, dark CURLY hair and a SHORT DARK BEARD. @Image7 IS THE ABSOLUTE AUTHORITY FOR TOMAS — his face, his collar, his cuffs, his coat and the black ribbon around him — AND IT OVERRIDES EVERY OTHER IMAGE AND EVERY WORD OF DESCRIPTION ON THAT SUBJECT. COPY HIS COSTUME FROM IT EXACTLY: a floor-length BLACK ROBE-COAT with ONE FLAT CREAM-OATMEAL LINEN PANEL down the centre front, TURNED-BACK CREAM CUFFS at both wrists, a TALL SMOOTH CYLINDRICAL CREAM COLLAR wrapped close around his throat with a level top edge — a smooth closed tube, never flared, never a wing, never a scallop, never two upright panels — and THE CLAUSE RIBBON, a long matte black band covered in fine pale engraved script, LOOPING AND SPIRALLING AROUND HIS BODY in large open curves and standing away from him in the air. THERE IS ONLY ONE TOMAS IN THIS FILM.

THE BREATH RULE — THE DEVICE OF THE WHOLE FILM: BEATRICE'S BREATH IS VISIBLE IN EVERY SHOT SHE IS IN. TOMAS'S BREATH: BEFORE HIS LAST SENTENCE IN SHOT 3, THE AIR IN FRONT OF HIS FACE IS COMPLETELY CLEAR AND TRANSPARENT; ON THAT SENTENCE A WHITE PLUME OF BREATH APPEARS IN FRONT OF HIS MOUTH AND HANGS IN THE COLD AIR. It is the only time he produces breath. NOBODY LOOKS AT IT, nobody mentions it, and the camera does not move toward it.

NOBODY RAISES THEIR VOICE, HURRIES, PLEADS OR SHOUTS. There is no build and no gathering of courage.

=== SHOT 1 — 0:00 to 0:07 — MEDIUM, 50mm, THE CAMERA GOES WITH HER ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
AMINA (off screen, from out on the pier, distant, urgent, unheroic): "Thirty per cent. Twenty-eight through. Twelve on the pier."

BEATRICE crosses the chamber to the slot rank, her right sleeve already pushed back, the frost on her knuckles and at her throat as in @Image4, and PUSHES HER RIGHT HAND INTO ONE OF THE SLOTS up to the wrist. She does it deliberately and unhurriedly. THE MOVE: the camera travels slowly and continuously with her toward the wall and keeps creeping after she stops. The worn trough slides past close to the lens.
THE SLOT IS DRAWING FROM HER: THE AMBER LIGHT INSIDE IT BEGINS TO DIM, and white begins at her nail beds. Her face stays calm. Her breath is visible.

CUT at 0:07.

=== SHOT 2 — 0:07 to 0:13 — CLOSE-UP, 85mm, LOCKED — ONE HAND OUT, ANOTHER IN ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
BEATRICE (off screen, one word): "Tomas."

Close on the slot in the dark granite with BEATRICE'S HAND IN IT, the light inside dimming. A MAN'S HAND enters from frame right — the BLACK SLEEVE and TURNED-BACK CREAM CUFF of a robe-coat at the wrist — CLOSES ON HER WRIST AND LIFTS HER HAND OUT OF THE WALL with the unhurried competence of a man closing a drawer. Her fingertips are white only at the nail beds. Her hand leaves the frame.
THEN HIS OWN HAND, cream cuff pushed back, GOES INTO THE SAME SLOT and stays there. THE SLOT'S DIM AMBER LIGHT COMES BACK UP TO ITS LEVEL AND HOLDS STEADY. HIS FINGERS STAY PINK. Nothing happens.

CUT at 0:13.

=== SHOT 3 — 0:13 to 0:22 — MEDIUM TWO-SHOT BY DEPTH, 40mm, SLOW PUSH — THE SENTENCE ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
TOMAS (flat, precise): "It cannot take what is not there."
BEATRICE: "Then come away from the wall."
TOMAS (he turns his head and looks at her; the same volume and the same voice he has used all day; he does not lean into it): "I would prefer you did not die."

TOMAS IS THE NEAR FIGURE: at FRAME RIGHT, CLOSE TO THE LENS AND LARGE, in sharp focus, his hand in the slot, warm amber on one side of his face and cold on the other; HIS TALL SMOOTH CREAM TUBE COLLAR AND THE LOOPING ENGRAVED RIBBON ARE PLAINLY VISIBLE AT THIS SIZE. BEATRICE IS THE FAR FIGURE: at FRAME LEFT, two metres deeper, a step back from the wall, holding the white fingertips of her right hand in her left, the starburst of rime at her throat, her breath visible. NEITHER OF THEM MOVES A STEP IN THIS SHOT. THE MOVE: the camera pushes in very slowly on the two of them, still advancing at the cut.
ON HIS LAST SENTENCE, A WHITE PLUME OF BREATH APPEARS IN FRONT OF HIS FACE. Beatrice does not reply.

CUT at 0:22.

=== SHOT 4 — 0:22 to 0:30 — CLOSE-UP MACRO, 100mm, ABSOLUTELY LOCKED — THE PRICE ===
SPOKEN IN THIS SHOT:
AMINA (off screen, distant, from the pier): "Rank's at full. Get them on."

Extreme close-up of HIS HAND IN THE SLOT, sharp, the black sleeve and cream cuff at the wrist. TWO THINGS HAPPEN AT ONCE, AT DIFFERENT DEPTHS, AND THE CAMERA STAYS ON THE NEAR ONE:
IN THE FOREGROUND, SHARP: THE AMBER LIGHT INSIDE THAT SLOT DIMS SMOOTHLY AND GOES COMPLETELY OUT, and HIS FINGERS BLANCH WHITE from the NAIL BEDS up to the second knuckle, with fine white rime forming outward from the knuckles.
IN THE TOP CORNER OF THE FRAME, DEEP AND OUT OF FOCUS, THE BRIGHT DOORWAY: it BEGINS as a DIM PALE GREY RECTANGLE and RISES SMOOTHLY TO A BLOWN-OUT GLARING WHITE and STAYS THAT WAY, with pale blurred shapes of people moving across it, boarding. THE CAMERA DOES NOT PAN, RACK OR REFRAME TOWARD IT.
AT THE MOMENT THE DOORWAY GOES WHITE, THE DRY TICKING STOPS and does not return; the silence reads as relief.
HOLD ON THE HAND. Then, at the very bottom edge of the frame, the hem of BEATRICE'S black coat and one boot step into the picture — ONE step toward him. CUT ON THAT STEP.

SOUND: flat cold wind at the doorway, cut off abruptly by the stone. A tight dry acoustic with NO reverb tail. The dry tick, stopping dead when the doorway goes white. A woman's voice calling numbers from outside, distant and flat. NO music, no score, no swells, no drone and no stingers at any point, and NO sound cue on the sentence or on the moment the slot takes.

Pronounce these words exactly and clearly: THIRTY, TWENTY-EIGHT, TWELVE, PREFER, RANK.

PALETTE: slot amber #A9721F, frost white #E9F1F4, worn stone #B9B1A2, doorway white #EEF3F5.

PHYSICS: cold injury behaves as real cold injury — white at the nail beds first, then up the finger, no reversal. FROST GROWS OUTWARD FROM BODIES AND NEVER INWARD FROM ANYTHING: it starts on a person's skin or clothes and its fine needles spread AWAY from them. The stone, the windows and the air never frost. Slot brightness only ever changes by dimmer. Nothing glows anywhere except the amber inside the slots. No machinery, no gears, no runes, no magical light, no lens flare, no particles, no smoke, no digital element, no screens, no interface, no signage, no ornament, and no Victorian, Edwardian, medieval or steampunk detail.
